fixes.explanation: The text doesn't say that, friend. It says Jehoshaphat "…had returned safely to his home in Jerusalem…" (2 Chronicles 19:1), and then Jehu goes out to confront him. What Jehu calls out is helping the wicked and loving those who hate the LORD (2 Chronicles 19:2). Running from battle never comes up.

Wrath is the word. Jehu says, “Because of this, the wrath of the LORD is upon you.” (2 Chronicles 19:2). Those are heavy words for a king to hear after he's back in Jerusalem. Hold on, though, because Jehu isn't done talking.

Peace sounds lovely, and I wish it fit here. Jehu says, “Because of this, the wrath of the LORD is upon you.” (2 Chronicles 19:2). It's a hard message, and the king hears it after he comes back to Jerusalem.

Yes! Jehu says, “…you have removed the Asherah poles from the land and have set your heart on seeking God.” (2 Chronicles 19:3). Jehu credits Jehoshaphat with removing those poles from the land. He says it right alongside the hard word, so both are on the table.

That's it. The text says he "…turned them back to the LORD, the God of their fathers." (2 Chronicles 19:4). That's a lot of ground, from Beersheba to the hill country of Ephraim. And the text says he went out "once again," so this wasn't the first time he went out among the people.

No armies get gathered here. The text says Jehoshaphat went out among the people and "…turned them back to the LORD, the God of their fathers." (2 Chronicles 19:4). Nothing in these verses says he's rounding up soldiers. This trip is about turning the people back to the LORD.

True! In Jerusalem, Jehoshaphat appointed “…some of the Levites, priests, and heads of the Israelite families to judge on behalf of the LORD and to settle disputes.” (2 Chronicles 19:8). So the priests are right there in the mix. It's a mixed group, with Levites, priests and family heads all named.

Not quite, friend. Jehoshaphat names bloodshed outright. He speaks of every dispute that comes before them, “…whether it regards bloodshed or some other violation of law, commandments, statutes, or ordinances…” (2 Chronicles 19:10). Bloodshed is on that list, so it isn't only small disputes.

Guilt is the word. The judges are to warn them “…so that they will not incur guilt before the LORD…” (2 Chronicles 19:10). Jehoshaphat adds that wrath won't come on the judges and their brothers either. Warning the people is part of the job.
